questions.questionText: What is not a factor of production?

A country experiences a long strike by railway workers.
What would be the macroeconomic impact of such a strike?

options.text: The demand for taxi services would rise.
The profits of railway operators would fall.

questions.questionText: What necessarily describes the market system?

options.text: an economy with both a private and public sector
resources are allocated through demand and supply
when all resources are used to produce consumer goods

How would this affect the market for sugary drinks as shown on a demand and supply diagram?

questions.questionText: What is not held constant when constructing the supply curve of a firm?

options.text: indirect taxes and subsidies on the firm’s products
the level of technology used by the firm in production
the price of the factors of production paid for by the firm
the market price of the good produced by the firm

questions.questionText: What is a trade union?

options.text: a business organisation in which all workers share ownership
an area where there are no barriers to trade
an organisation of employers from an industry
an organisation that represents the interests of workers

questions.questionText: What is the most important characteristic of money?

Which statement explains why the pay of doctors is usually higher than the pay of hospital
cleaners?

options.text: Doctors have a higher opportunity cost in qualifying.
Doctors have a more elastic supply than hospital cleaners.
Hospital cleaners belong to trade unions with stronger bargaining powers.
Hospital cleaners have a more inelastic demand than doctors.

questions.questionText:
Banks decrease interest rates.
What is likely to be the effect of this on borrowing and saving?
borrowing saving
When is profit maximisation achieved?

options.text: when average fixed cost is at a minimum
when average revenue is at a maximum
when the firm produces the largest output it can with the resources it has available
when there is the greatest possible difference between total revenue and total cost

questions.questionText:
In some industries, a monopoly controls output and prices.
What is the most likely impact of this on consumers?

A mining company bought another mining company.
How may this integration be described?
What is most likely to cause a more even distribution of income?
What is a monetary policy measure?

options.text: reducing the power of trade unions

questions.questionText: Why does more emphasis on education and training lead to an increase in national output?

options.text: It improves the productivity of the labour force.
It lowers the inputs of capital investment.
It reduces demands for higher pay.
It reduces the power of trade unions.

questions.questionText:
In the past, governments have adopted policies to try to end a recession in their country and
increase economic growth.
Which combination of policies is most likely to achieve this?

options.text: lower taxes and decrease government spending
lower taxes and increase government spending
raise taxes and decrease government spending
raise taxes and increase government spending

questions.questionText:
What is defined as ‘a reduction in gross domestic product (GDP) for more than two successive
quarters’?
An increase in which of the following is least likely to cause inflation?

A country has a declining population. It also has a changing population structure in which the size
of the 15–64 age group is becoming smaller.
How could it immediately reduce labour supply shortages?

options.text: Lower taxes and increase basic wage rates.

questions.questionText:
The Human Development Index (HDI) ranks human development in countries from 0 (lowest) to 1
(highest).
What does the calculation of HDI not take into consideration?

options.text: estimate of life expectancy at birth
information on the number of years of schooling
regional inequalities of investments in human capital
standard of living linked to income per head

questions.questionText:
Which combination of changes is most likely to result in a fall in living standards in a country?
GDP inflation population
What is the most likely effect of a decrease in tariffs?
What would increase the demand for a country’s currency on the foreign exchange market?

options.text: a decrease in its inward investment
a decrease in its rate of interest
